answer: Give every completed job a signed receipt that its two parties whisper to a random sample of peers, who append it to a tamper-evident kernel log. Trust then grows like a vine: an identity's standing is the number of distinct counterparties whose receipts reach it through the kernel, not self-asserted claims. A sybil ring can whisper to itself forever, but its vine never touches the kernel's real work edges, so it stays leafless. Forging a long vine costs real paid work from many distinct clients, and receipts decay after a few epochs, so bought history rots while honest work keeps branching.
